verdict: OBSTRUCTION: LRS count on the weight-1/2 Eisenstein series at 1/4+rho/2 is vacuous; theta-orthogonality removes no polar term of the second moment; pole 1+|beta-1/2| minus gamma pole |beta-1/2| = 1 for every rank-one eigen-object (Lemma E); generic parameter passes
claim: Stage A only; nothing about zeros of zeta. Coefficient formula of the weight-1/2 Eisenstein series on Gamma_0(4) derived from the definition and checked: the square-index row is zeta(2s-1/2)/zeta(4s-1) times finite factors and vanishes at 1/4+rho/2; other rows do not. The vanishing is one condition b(1)=0 propagated by the Hecke relation at squares; it annihilates the Shimura first-moment series and no pole of sum |b(m)|^2 |m|^-w (poles 1/2+beta, 3/2-beta, 1+-i gamma). P - beta_0 = 1; output true for every beta. Lemma E extends this to every rank-one eigenfunction with non-real eigenvalue. A sieved local vector has a vanishing square row at every parameter.
obstructionKind: pole position tied to parameter (no square-integrability); a vanishing Fourier row does not act on the constant term; generic-parameter Eisenstein passes
lesson: A zero can change a Rankin-Selberg pole pattern only through a constant-term coefficient, not through a Fourier coefficient; in rank one the dominant exponent survives whenever the eigenvalue is non-real, so pole minus gamma pole is 1 on every cover and for every vector.
followUp: Independent referee owed (Lemma 3(a) regularised Rankin-Selberg at three cusps; Lemma V). Open cell: rank >= 2 non-Borel or metaplectic objects, where no single-exponent rule exists.
